To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) exposure of scleral buckle is an important complication of retinal reattachment surgery; (2) it occurs most often in the first six months postoperatively; (3) it is more common after temporal buckling; (4) it occurs more often with anteriorly placed implants; (5) it occurs more with large implants; (6) it occurs more frequently with thin sclera; (7) it occurs more commonly with multiple operations; and 8)
the exposure process is associated with an anteriorly placed, temporal, large scleral implant, thin sclera, multiple operations, and bacterial contamination.
the incidence of exposed intrascleral implants is low, but the complications associated with their removal can be severe.

an intrasclerally placed implant should be removed as soon as possible after it is exposed.
